 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 04.06.2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
Manjunatha .S.H vs Praveen Kumar .N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122792537/

sentences.text:
On 04.06.2023 at about 1.20 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-EZ- 4806 from Chikkabanavara to Hesaragatta, when he reached near Sai MRP Bar shop Thore Nagasandra cross, Hesaraghatta main road,
Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 proceeding at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner from opposite direction and caused the accident.
Due to that impact all the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 49 years, doing agriculture and tailoring work and earning Rs.39,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
It is alleged that the respondent is the owner of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

3. After service of notice the respondent-owner has appeared through his counsel and filed written statement by admitting that he is the registered owner of the offending Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 and he has got the said Car insured with the Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
Bengaluru branch, however the said insurance policy was not renewed due to the lapse of the company policy stating that the online payment was not accepted and as such the respondent had waited till the payment duly received by the insurance company and to renew the said policy.
He has denied the cause and manner of accident and also the involvement of the offending Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 in the alleged accident.
Further he has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is too excessive, exorbitant.
By denying the alleged negligence the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against him.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 as as a result, he sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner proves the age and earnings of the petitioner as stated in the claim petition ?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much?
4. What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 18.

Further examined the Dr.Chetan A.,
Orthopaedic surgeon at Hosmat Hospital was examined as PW.2 and got marked the Manjunatha .S.H vs Praveen Kumar .N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122792537/
2 documents at Ex.P19 to Ex.P23.
The respondent does not chosen to lead any evidence.
6. Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.
The respondent not canvassed the arguments, hence the case is posted for judgment with liberty to file written arguments by serving the copy to opposite party.
On 03.09.2025 the respondent filed written arguments by posting the copy of written arguments to the petitioner through post.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the partly affirmative

Issue No.3 : In the affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.
As per the documents produced by the petitioner Ex.P1- FIR is came to be registered on the basis of first information given by one Madhusudhan.
In the said complaint, the first informant alleged the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing No.KA-04- MD-5352.

After registration of FIR the IO has prepared spot mahazar and spot sketch as per Ex.P3 and P.4.
11.
Immediately after the accident, the IO conducted spot mahazar and rough sketch as per Ex.P3 and P.4.
On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 and P.4 spot mahazar and sketch the description of the accident spot is in the left side of the road in which the petitioner was proceeding.
As per the sketch and mahazar the offending car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 came from opposite side and by coming to the wrong side dashed against three motorcycles.

The rough sketch and mahazar marked at Ex.P3 and P.4 establishes the negligence of the driver of car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352.
12.

The contents of Ex.P3 & 4 mahazar and rough sketch evidentiates that the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 was rash and negligent in his driving and supported the petitioner to Manjunatha .S.H vs Praveen Kumar .N

on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122792537/
3 prove the alleged negligence of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-04-MD- 5352.
If the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA- 04-MD-5352 proceeded in his left side portion of the road the said accident was not going to be caused.

13. Further Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein the Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 has got damages in its front bumper, bonnet, right side front fender, right side headlight, front wind screen glass cracked, right side front wheel disc, right side rear view mirror.
On the other hand the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-EZ-4806 got damages in its front shape.
The Ex.P.6 IMV report prima facie establishes that the offending car bearing No.KA-04- MD-5352 got its major damages in its front right side.
This shows that the driver of car bearing No.KA-04-MD- 5352 came to his extreme right side/wrong side and caused the accident.
Thereby the contents of spot mahazar, sketch and IMV report prima facie establishes the negligence of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-04-MD- 5352.
In this accident the offending car dashed against three motorcycles which evidentiates the negligence of the driver of the car.
14. In the accident cases, it is settled principle of law that "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" which means the things speaks itself, is the standing principle to know the nature of the accident.
Under this principle how the negligence has to be infer is considered.

In tort law, "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" principle that allows petitioners to meet their burden of proof with under which a court can infer negligence from the very nature of an accident or injury in the absence of direct evidence on how any defendant behaved in the context of tort litigation.

On perusal of Ex.P3- contents of mahazar and Ex.P.4 rough sketch along with Ex.P6 IMV report wherein the damages of the vehicles involved in the accident is mentioned prima- facie shows the negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352.

If the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 was in controllable speed and proceeded in his left side portion of the road and if he was not negligent he could have controlled his vehicle and the alleged accident would not happened.

15. The Ex.P7 is the charge sheet was came to be filed against the driver of Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC and under Sec.146, 196,
56, 192 of MV Act wherein the IO after detailed investigation has found that there is a negligence on the part of driver of Car bearing No.KA-04- MD-5352 for the accident.
No other grounds and independent evidence are produced by the respondent to prove the contrary to the opinion of the IO as per Ex.P7 charge sheet.
As per the reasons discussed above no supporting evidence is available to accept the defence of the respondent .
16. The PW1 is the injured and eyewitness who alleges the negligence of driver of car bearing No.KA-04- MD-5352.
At the time of cross-examination of PW1 it was suggested to the PW1 that he himself dashed against the ahead going motorcycle.
The said suggestion was denied by the PW1.
Against the said defence no evidence is placed by the respondent.
The contents of Ex.P.3 mahazar and P.4 rough sketch falsifies the said defence of the respondent.
As per Ex.P.3 mahazar and P.4 rough sketch the offending car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352 came to its extreme right side and caused the accident.
The accident spot as per rough sketch and mahazar is in the left side portion of the road.
Thus, no grounds are made to consider the negligence or contributory negligence of the petitioner.
Manjunatha .S.H vs Praveen Kumar .N

on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122792537/
4 17.
The fact of accident is established before this tribunal.

The Ex.P6 which is the wound certificate also establishes that the petitioner sustained injuries in the said RTA dated 04.06.2023.
18.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MD-5352.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 & 3 :
As these two issues are interlinked with each other in respect of entitlement of the petitioner in claiming the compensation they are taken together for common discussion.
20. As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MD- 5352.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 49 years.
As per Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P16 the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 20.07.1974.
The accident was took place on 04.06.2023.
Hence as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 49 years.
The petitioner has produced Discharge Summary marked at Ex.P8.

As per Ex.P8 the petitioner was admitted to Hosmat hospital from 04.06.2023 to 10.06.2023, and has sustained Right femur sub trochanteric fracture and has also underwent ORIF with 14 hole DHS done on 05.06.2023 under SA.
By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.40,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bill as per Ex.P12 amounting to Rs.2,13,183/- and Ex.P.17 amounting to Rs.7,676/- which are supported by medical prescription at Manjunatha .S.H vs Praveen Kumar .N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122792537/
5 Ex.P14 and also discharge summary marked at Ex.P.8.
The medical bill is not seriously disputed by the respondent and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bill.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off the same i.e., Rs. 2,20,900/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that he was doing agriculture and Tailoring and earning Rs.39,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has produced has not produced any documents.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered in the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8 - the petitioner was admitted to Hosmat hospital from 04.06.2023 to 10.06.2023 for the period of 7 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total 4 months period including 7 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months = Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.
Chetan A., Orthopaedic Surgeon at Hosmat Hospital as PW.2 and through him Inpatient case details, outpatient records, future medical estimation, medical bill and X-ray were got marked at Ex.P19 & 23.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained Comminuted subtrochanteric fracture of right femur.
As per the evidence of PW2 doctor the petitioner sustained lower limb disability of 44% and whole body disability of 15%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross- examination.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
The fractures are united and implants are in situ.
A perusal of the injuries sustained, treatment taken, it is considered that though the petitioner is having 15% permanent physical whole body disability.
The injuries is on right femur.
The fracture to right lower limb will certainly effects the day to day work of the petitioner.
Hence considering all these aspects this tribunal has taken disability at 13%.

The petitioner has stated that he was doing Agriculture and Tailoring work and earning Rs.39,000/-
p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
To consider the avocation of the petitioner except the oral evidence, no documents or proof of salary is shown by the petitioner.
Such being the case it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2023.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '13'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 13 X 13% =Rs.3,24,480/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P8 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 7 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P8 the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
Petitioners have also produced 5 Ambulance bills at Ex.P13 total of Rs.28,300/-.

By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the Manjunatha .S.H vs Praveen Kumar .N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122792537/
6 pain and other allied effects of the accident and looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injury sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards food and nourishment,
conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injury in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 5 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.7,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 7 days in the hospital.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses: PW2 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants in right femur and he estimated cost for the surgery is about Rs.1,00,000/-.
Hence, Rs.45,000/- is awarded under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 40,000/- b.
Towards medical expenses Rs. 2,20,900/-

c. Towards loss of income during Rs. 64,000/-
laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 3,24,480/- e.

Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 40,000/-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 7,000/- g.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/- h.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 45,000/-
Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondent in his objection statement has admitted that there is no insurance policy to the offending vehicle.

Even though it is suggested to PW1 that the accident was caused by his negligence, the said defence is not accepted for the reasons discussed in Issue No.1.
35.
The respondent himself admitted that insurance policy was lapsed as on the date of accident.
It is further contended that the insurance policy was not renewed due to lapse of the company as it has not accepted the online payment.
The said defence itself establishes that there was no contract between the respondent and insurance company.

As there is no valid policy as on the date of accident, as such the Manjunatha .S.H vs Praveen Kumar .N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122792537/
7 respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner along with interest @
6% p.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered in the partly affirmative and Issue No.3 is answered in the affirmative by holding that the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as discussed above.

ISSUE NO.3:
22.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.7,71,380/- (Rupees Seven lakhs seventy one thousand three hundred and eighty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on the computer, corrected by me and then pro nounced in the open court on this the 4th day of September 2025) (Kanchi Mayanna Goutam)
